verdict:
# Disqualify: Salesforce PRM (Partner Cloud)

**1. Missing / unproven requirement**
The gate is not met (p=0.15). Deal registration and lead routing are claimed ([salesforce.com/sales/partner-relationship-management](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/partner-relationship-management/)), and field-level sync via Partner Connect is described — but **no expiry, denial, or re-routing rules are evidenced**, and **onboarding approval workflows are not evidenced** ([AI PRM page](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/partner-relationship-management/ai-prm/) mentions onboarding automation only in passing). A competing vendor states companies "end up moving to Channeltivity" for out-of-the-box channel functionality ([help.channeltivity.com](https://help.channeltivity.com/support/solutions/articles/3000016461-salesforce-integration-deal-registration-overview)).

**2. Real gap, or missing evidence?**
Probably missing evidence, not a product gap — Salesforce's platform can build expiry/denial via Flow and custom objects, but nothing documented out of the box. **One question:** *Show a documented, OOTB deal-registration flow with expiry and denial/reassignment, plus a multi-step partner onboarding approval — with source links.*

**3. When to still look**
As an AI/enablement layer alongside a purpose-built PRM, or if the team accepts building deal-reg governance natively. Not for distributor multi-tier — not evidenced.

## Closing the partial / not-evidenced areas

- **Partner experience & UI (partial)** — configure: personalized Experience Cloud templates are in-platform ([SF PRM](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/partner-relationship-management/)).
- **Partner onboarding (partial)** — configure the lifecycle; approval gates are not evidenced, so build them as Salesforce Flows.
- **Partner enablement (partial)** — configure/enable in the Partner Ecosystem Management tier ($50/member/mo, adds enablement & loyalty).
- **MDF management (partial)** — configure fund/campaign requests and in-Salesforce approval; allocation and sharing rules need build.
- **Deal registration (partial)** — configure on native Lead/Opportunity; expiry and denial routing not evidenced → build, or bolt on Channeltivity (bi-directional SF sync, [docs](https://help.channeltivity.com/support/solutions/articles/3000016461-salesforce-integration-deal-registration-overview)).
- **Reporting (partial)** — configure: dashboards/reports feed directly from CRM; channel-specific analytics is build work.
- **Admin & controls (partial)** — configure: permissions for partners and internal teams; finer governance not evidenced.
- **Distributor & multi-tier (not evidenced)** — nothing in evidence; integrate a multi-tier tool or build custom objects.
- **Migration & vendor risk (not evidenced)** — no migration tooling evidenced; build ETL into Salesforce objects so history stays in the SoR.

## Verdict: buy and extend

Salesforce PRM is the only option here with evidenced native Salesforce SoR sync and an AI partner assistant, so buying that base and building the unmet hard requirements (deal-reg expiry/denial, onboarding approvals, multi-tier, MDF allocation) on Salesforce avoids a second data store and a second integration. Maintenance becomes admin/Flow work rather than vendor lock-in, and $25–$50/member/mo undercuts rebuilding a portal plus AI — but hard requirements remain unmet today (p=0.15), so budget the build before signing.

# Best PRM Software in 2026

An honest comparison of the best PRM (partner relationship management) software in 2026 — pricing, CRM integrations, and who each tool is really for.

PRM (Partner Relationship Management) software — also called partner management software or channel partner software — helps you run partner programs — referral, reseller, affiliate, and channel — with a real system behind onboarding, deal registration, partner portals, enablement content, and reporting. If your CRM is built for your direct sales team, a PRM is the equivalent system for your partners.

TL;DR: There’s no single “best PRM software” — the right pick depends on your program size, price sensitivity, and partner motion. Here are the best PRM software options in 2026, grouped by the job they do best:

* Best PRM for SMBs & startups: PartnerPortal, Kiflo
* Best PRM for CRM coverage: PartnerPortal
* Best AI-native PRM: Introw
* Best PRM for many partner types: JourneyBee
* Best PRM for affiliate & referral scale: PartnerStack
* Best PRM for Salesforce/Dynamics customization: Magentrix
* Best PRM for Salesforce: Salesforce PRM
* Best enterprise PRM: Impartner, ZINFI, Unifyr, Allbound / ChannelScaler

## How we picked the best PRM software (methodology)

We didn’t rank on feature-count or on who has the flashiest AI messaging. We weighted four things a real buyer actually lives with:

1. Is it a real PRM? Full partner lifecycle — onboarding, deal/lead registration, portal, enablement, reporting — not just an affiliate-link tracker.
2. CRM integration depth. What actually syncs, how reliably, and which CRMs (not just Salesforce and HubSpot).
3. Time-to-value. Can a normal team launch in days, or does it need a services project and a quarter?
4. Fit for your size and motion. The best enterprise PRM is the wrong tool for most Startups and SMBs, and vice versa.

We deliberately kept the list to genuine PRMs and clearly labeled the edge cases. We didn’t pad it out with affiliate-only tools to hit a bigger number — see Tools we deliberately didn’t rank at the end.

## What changed in PRM software in 2026

* CRM-native is the new baseline. Buyers increasingly expect the PRM to live inside their CRM’s data, not maintain a separate copy — and increasingly for CRMs beyond Salesforce/HubSpot.
* Co-selling over static deal registration. More programs are collaborative (shared pipeline, account mapping) rather than one-way lead submission.
* Off-portal engagement. Slack/Teams/email delivery to fight the “portal nobody logs into” problem.
* Faster deployment expectations. “Launch in days” is now table stakes for SMB/mid-market; multi-month implementations are an enterprise-only tolerance.

## How to choose the right PRM software (fast)

PRM software selection gets simpler once you answer a few questions:

1. Which CRM do you use — and how deep must the integration be? (native two-way sync vs. occasional export; Salesforce/HubSpot vs. Pipedrive/Zoho/Attio)
2. What partner motion are you running? (referral, reseller, affiliate, co-sell, distributor)
3. What’s your budget? (a free or sub-$300/mo tool for an SMB program, mid-market at ~$250–$2,000/mo, or enterprise at $20k+/yr plus implementation — see the most affordable PRMs if price is the deciding factor)
4. How fast do you need to launch? (live this week vs. a multi-month rollout with services)
5. How much complexity and governance do you actually need? (a clean portal + deal registration vs. MDF/TCMA, partner tiers, and global-channel controls)

One-sentence heuristic:

* Need enterprise channel governance? Buy an enterprise PRM.
* Need SaaS partner growth at scale? PartnerStack is usually on the shortlist.
* Need a partner portal that launches quickly and integrates deeply with your CRM? Prioritize speed + integration depth over feature bloat.

Modified on Tue, 3 Feb at 2:33 PM

This article provides an overview of Channeltivity’s Deal Registration integration with Salesforce. Please also see the Deal Registration Salesforce Integration Setup instructions.

Channeltivity’s Deal Registration integration with Salesforce makes it easy to get your Partners’ registered Deals from Channeltivity into your Salesforce CRM. Following the illustration below, the integration can be explained in three steps:

1. **Channeltivity Deal Submission and Salesforce Record Creation** - Once a Partner submits a new Deal registration, Channeltivity creates a copy of the registered Deal as a Lead within Salesforce. This can be configured to happen manually or automatically based on creation or approval status. 
   * **(Optional Setting)** **Opportunity Creation via Contact Match:** If enabled, Channeltivity will attempt to match the End User Contact on the Deal to an existing Salesforce Contact **using the email address**. If exactly**one match is found**, an Opportunity is created instead of a Lead. If no match is found, a Lead is created.
2. **Ongoing Sync** - Changes made to the Deal in Channeltivity are reflected in Salesforce and vice versa.
3. **Lead Conversion Handling** - Should you decide to convert a Salesforce Lead to an Opportunity, Channeltivity will recognize this and maintain the link to the corresponding record.

### Can Salesforce Opportunities be imported into Channeltivity as Deals?

Yes, Salesforce Opportunities can be imported into Channeltivity as Deal Registrations. Learn more about this topic here: How do I create Deal Registrations from Salesforce Opportunities in my PRM?. 

### Is the integration bi-directional?

Yes, the Deal Registration integration is a true bi-bidirectional integration. Your Deal Registration integration field mappings allow you to determine the data flow between the Deal in Channeltivity and the corresponding Lead/Opportunity in Salesforce. 

### When is a Deal synced to Salesforce?

You can configure the Deal Registration integration settings to sync new Deals to Salesforce manually or automatically based on specific events.

  + Created

By default, Channeltivity creates Leads rather than Opportunities. Channeltivity’s Deal Registration integration with Salesforce makes it easy to get your Partners’ registered Deals from Channeltivity into your Salesforce CRM. Following the illustration below, the integration can be explained in three steps:

1. **Channeltivity Deal Submission and Salesforce Record Creation** - Once a Partner submits a new Deal registration, Channeltivity creates a copy of the registered Deal as a Lead within Salesforce. This can be configured to happen manually or automatically based on creation or approval status. 
   * **(Optional Setting)** **Opportunity Creation via Contact Match:** If enabled, Channeltivity will attempt to match the End User Contact on the Deal to an existing Salesforce Contact **using the email address**. If exactly**one match is found**, an Opportunity is created instead of a Lead. If no match is found, a Lead is created.
2. **Ongoing Sync** - Changes made to the Deal in Channeltivity are reflected in Salesforce and vice versa.
3. **Lead Conversion Handling** - Should you decide to convert a Salesforce Lead to an Opportunity, Channeltivity will recognize this and maintain the link to the corresponding record.

## FAQs:

### Can Salesforce Opportunities be imported into Channeltivity as Deals?

Yes, Salesforce Opportunities can be imported into Channeltivity as Deal Registrations. Learn more about this topic here: How do I create Deal Registrations from Salesforce Opportunities in my PRM?. 

### Is the integration bi-directional?

Yes, the Deal Registration integration is a true bi-bidirectional integration. Your Deal Registration integration field mappings allow you to determine the data flow between the Deal in Channeltivity and the corresponding Lead/Opportunity in Salesforce. 

### When is a Deal synced to Salesforce?

You can configure the Deal Registration integration settings to sync new Deals to Salesforce manually or automatically based on specific events.  

* **Manual:**Requires an Internal User to manually sync the Deal to Salesforce by clicking the Salesforce button on the Deal in Channeltivity > Sync .
* **Event-Based** (Automatic)**:**Deals are automatically synced to Salesforce when a selected event occurs:
  + Created
  + Pre-Approved
  + Approved

### When does Channeltivity create a Lead vs. an Opportunity in Salesforce?

By default, Channeltivity creates Leads rather than Opportunities. The reason Channeltivity creates Leads instead of Opportunities is because Opportunities have to be associated with an Account and Contact in Salesforce, and every company has its own unique guidelines for establishing those associations. Since the rules vary across companies, we felt it was best to create Leads instead of Opportunities to allow Users to select the relevant Account/Contact when converting the Lead to an Opportunity.

# Best PRM Software in 2026

An honest comparison of the best PRM (partner relationship management) software in 2026 — pricing, CRM integrations, and who each tool is really for.

PRM (Partner Relationship Management) software — also called partner management software or channel partner software — helps you run partner programs — referral, reseller, affiliate, and channel — with a real system behind onboarding, deal registration, partner portals, enablement content, and reporting. If your CRM is built for your direct sales team, a PRM is the equivalent system for your partners.

TL;DR: There’s no single “best PRM software” — the right pick depends on your program size, price sensitivity, and partner motion. Here are the best PRM software options in 2026, grouped by the job they do best:

* Best PRM for SMBs & startups: PartnerPortal, Kiflo
* Best PRM for CRM coverage: PartnerPortal
* Best AI-native PRM: Introw
* Best PRM for many partner types: JourneyBee
* Best PRM for affiliate & referral scale: PartnerStack
* Best PRM for Salesforce/Dynamics customization: Magentrix
* Best PRM for Salesforce: Salesforce PRM
* Best enterprise PRM: Impartner, ZINFI, Unifyr, Allbound / ChannelScaler

## How we picked the best PRM software (methodology)

We didn’t rank on feature-count or on who has the flashiest AI messaging. We weighted four things a real buyer actually lives with:

1. Is it a real PRM? Full partner lifecycle — onboarding, deal/lead registration, portal, enablement, reporting — not just an affiliate-link tracker.
2. CRM integration depth. What actually syncs, how reliably, and which CRMs (not just Salesforce and HubSpot).
3. Time-to-value. Can a normal team launch in days, or does it need a services project and a quarter?
4. Fit for your size and motion. The best enterprise PRM is the wrong tool for most Startups and SMBs, and vice versa.

We deliberately kept the list to genuine PRMs and clearly labeled the edge cases. We didn’t pad it out with affiliate-only tools to hit a bigger number — see Tools we deliberately didn’t rank at the end.

## What changed in PRM software in 2026

* CRM-native is the new baseline. Buyers increasingly expect the PRM to live inside their CRM’s data, not maintain a separate copy — and increasingly for CRMs beyond Salesforce/HubSpot.
* Co-selling over static deal registration. More programs are collaborative (shared pipeline, account mapping) rather than one-way lead submission.
* Off-portal engagement. Slack/Teams/email delivery to fight the “portal nobody logs into” problem.
* Faster deployment expectations. “Launch in days” is now table stakes for SMB/mid-market; multi-month implementations are an enterprise-only tolerance.

## How to choose the right PRM software (fast)

PRM software selection gets simpler once you answer a few questions:

1. Which CRM do you use — and how deep must the integration be? (native two-way sync vs. occasional export; Salesforce/HubSpot vs. Pipedrive/Zoho/Attio)
2. What partner motion are you running? (referral, reseller, affiliate, co-sell, distributor)
3. What’s your budget? (a free or sub-$300/mo tool for an SMB program, mid-market at ~$250–$2,000/mo, or enterprise at $20k+/yr plus implementation — see the most affordable PRMs if price is the deciding factor)
4. How fast do you need to launch? (live this week vs. a multi-month rollout with services)
5. How much complexity and governance do you actually need? (a clean portal + deal registration vs. MDF/TCMA, partner tiers, and global-channel controls)

One-sentence heuristic:

* Need enterprise channel governance? Buy an enterprise PRM.
* Need SaaS partner growth at scale? PartnerStack is usually on the shortlist.
* Need a partner portal that launches quickly and integrates deeply with your CRM? Prioritize speed + integration depth over feature bloat.

# Salesforce Integration: Deal Registration - Overview

Modified on Tue, 3 Feb at 2:33 PM

This article provides an overview of Channeltivity’s Deal Registration integration with Salesforce. Please also see the Deal Registration Salesforce Integration Setup instructions.

Channeltivity’s Deal Registration integration with Salesforce makes it easy to get your Partners’ registered Deals from Channeltivity into your Salesforce CRM. Following the illustration below, the integration can be explained in three steps:

1. **Channeltivity Deal Submission and Salesforce Record Creation** - Once a Partner submits a new Deal registration, Channeltivity creates a copy of the registered Deal as a Lead within Salesforce. This can be configured to happen manually or automatically based on creation or approval status. 
   * **(Optional Setting)** **Opportunity Creation via Contact Match:** If enabled, Channeltivity will attempt to match the End User Contact on the Deal to an existing Salesforce Contact **using the email address**. If exactly**one match is found**, an Opportunity is created instead of a Lead. If no match is found, a Lead is created.
2. **Ongoing Sync** - Changes made to the Deal in Channeltivity are reflected in Salesforce and vice versa.
3. **Lead Conversion Handling** - Should you decide to convert a Salesforce Lead to an Opportunity, Channeltivity will recognize this and maintain the link to the corresponding record.

## FAQs:

### Can Salesforce Opportunities be imported into Channeltivity as Deals?

Yes, Salesforce Opportunities can be imported into Channeltivity as Deal Registrations. Learn more about this topic here: How do I create Deal Registrations from Salesforce Opportunities in my PRM?. 

### Is the integration bi-directional?

Yes, the Deal Registration integration is a true bi-bidirectional integration. Your Deal Registration integration field mappings allow you to determine the data flow between the Deal in Channeltivity and the corresponding Lead/Opportunity in Salesforce. 

### When is a Deal synced to Salesforce?

You can configure the Deal Registration integration settings to sync new Deals to Salesforce manually or automatically based on specific events.  

* **Manual:**Requires an Internal User to manually sync the Deal to Salesforce by clicking the Salesforce button on the Deal in Channeltivity > Sync .
* **Event-Based** (Automatic)**:**Deals are automatically synced to Salesforce when a selected event occurs:
  + Created
  + Pre-Approved
  + Approved

### When does Channeltivity create a Lead vs. an Opportunity in Salesforce?

By default, Channeltivity creates Leads rather than Opportunities. The reason Channeltivity creates Leads instead of Opportunities is because Opportunities have to be associated with an Account and Contact in Salesforce, and every company has its own unique guidelines for establishing those associations. Since the rules vary across companies, we felt it was best to create Leads instead of Opportunities to allow Users to select the relevant Account/Contact when converting the Lead to an Opportunity. 

However, Channeltivity also offers an optional setting that, when enabled, Channeltivity will attempt to match the End User Contact on the Deal to an existing Salesforce Contact based on email. If exactly one match is found, an Opportunity is created instead of a Lead. If no match is found, a Lead is created. For more information on this topic check out this article.

An honest comparison of the best PRM (partner relationship management) software in 2026 — pricing, CRM integrations, and who each tool is really for.

PRM (Partner Relationship Management) software — also called partner management software or channel partner software — helps you run partner programs — referral, reseller, affiliate, and channel — with a real system behind onboarding, deal registration, partner portals, enablement content, and reporting. If your CRM is built for your direct sales team, a PRM is the equivalent system for your partners.

TL;DR: There’s no single “best PRM software” — the right pick depends on your program size, price sensitivity, and partner motion. Here are the best PRM software options in 2026, grouped by the job they do best:

## How we picked the best PRM software (methodology)

We didn’t rank on feature-count or on who has the flashiest AI messaging. We weighted four things a real buyer actually lives with:

1. Is it a real PRM? Full partner lifecycle — onboarding, deal/lead registration, portal, enablement, reporting — not just an affiliate-link tracker.
2. CRM integration depth. What actually syncs, how reliably, and which CRMs (not just Salesforce and HubSpot).
3. Time-to-value. Can a normal team launch in days, or does it need a services project and a quarter?
4. Fit for your size and motion. The best enterprise PRM is the wrong tool for most Startups and SMBs, and vice versa.

We deliberately kept the list to genuine PRMs and clearly labeled the edge cases. We didn’t pad it out with affiliate-only tools to hit a bigger number — see Tools we deliberately didn’t rank at the end.

## What changed in PRM software in 2026

* Co-selling over static deal registration. More programs are collaborative (shared pipeline, account mapping) rather than one-way lead submission.
* Off-portal engagement. Slack/Teams/email delivery to fight the “portal nobody logs into” problem.
* Faster deployment expectations. “Launch in days” is now table stakes for SMB/mid-market; multi-month implementations are an enterprise-only tolerance.

# Salesforce Integration: Deal Registration - Overview

Modified on Tue, 3 Feb at 2:33 PM

This article provides an overview of Channeltivity’s Deal Registration integration with Salesforce. Please also see the Deal Registration Salesforce Integration Setup instructions.

Channeltivity’s Deal Registration integration with Salesforce makes it easy to get your Partners’ registered Deals from Channeltivity into your Salesforce CRM. Following the illustration below, the integration can be explained in three steps:

1. **Channeltivity Deal Submission and Salesforce Record Creation** - Once a Partner submits a new Deal registration, Channeltivity creates a copy of the registered Deal as a Lead within Salesforce. This can be configured to happen manually or automatically based on creation or approval status. 
   * **(Optional Setting)** **Opportunity Creation via Contact Match:** If enabled, Channeltivity will attempt to match the End User Contact on the Deal to an existing Salesforce Contact **using the email address**. If exactly**one match is found**, an Opportunity is created instead of a Lead. If no match is found, a Lead is created.
2. **Ongoing Sync** - Changes made to the Deal in Channeltivity are reflected in Salesforce and vice versa.
3. **Lead Conversion Handling** - Should you decide to convert a Salesforce Lead to an Opportunity, Channeltivity will recognize this and maintain the link to the corresponding record.

## FAQs:

### Can Salesforce Opportunities be imported into Channeltivity as Deals?

Yes, Salesforce Opportunities can be imported into Channeltivity as Deal Registrations. Learn more about this topic here: How do I create Deal Registrations from Salesforce Opportunities in my PRM?. 

### Is the integration bi-directional?

Yes, the Deal Registration integration is a true bi-bidirectional integration. Your Deal Registration integration field mappings allow you to determine the data flow between the Deal in Channeltivity and the corresponding Lead/Opportunity in Salesforce. 

### When is a Deal synced to Salesforce?

You can configure the Deal Registration integration settings to sync new Deals to Salesforce manually or automatically based on specific events.  

* **Manual:**Requires an Internal User to manually sync the Deal to Salesforce by clicking the Salesforce button on the Deal in Channeltivity > Sync .
* **Event-Based** (Automatic)**:**Deals are automatically synced to Salesforce when a selected event occurs:
  + Created
  + Pre-Approved
  + Approved

### When does Channeltivity create a Lead vs. an Opportunity in Salesforce?

By default, Channeltivity creates Leads rather than Opportunities. The reason Channeltivity creates Leads instead of Opportunities is because Opportunities have to be associated with an Account and Contact in Salesforce, and every company has its own unique guidelines for establishing those associations. Since the rules vary across companies, we felt it was best to create Leads instead of Opportunities to allow Users to select the relevant Account/Contact when converting the Lead to an Opportunity. 

However, Channeltivity also offers an optional setting that, when enabled, Channeltivity will attempt to match the End User Contact on the Deal to an existing Salesforce Contact based on email. If exactly one match is found, an Opportunity is created instead of a Lead. If no match is found, a Lead is created. For more information on this topic check out this article.

# Salesforce Integration: Deal Registration - Overview

Modified on Tue, 3 Feb at 2:33 PM

This article provides an overview of Channeltivity’s Deal Registration integration with Salesforce. Please also see the Deal Registration Salesforce Integration Setup instructions.

Channeltivity’s Deal Registration integration with Salesforce makes it easy to get your Partners’ registered Deals from Channeltivity into your Salesforce CRM. Following the illustration below, the integration can be explained in three steps:

1. **Channeltivity Deal Submission and Salesforce Record Creation** - Once a Partner submits a new Deal registration, Channeltivity creates a copy of the registered Deal as a Lead within Salesforce. This can be configured to happen manually or automatically based on creation or approval status. 
   * **(Optional Setting)** **Opportunity Creation via Contact Match:** If enabled, Channeltivity will attempt to match the End User Contact on the Deal to an existing Salesforce Contact **using the email address**. If exactly**one match is found**, an Opportunity is created instead of a Lead. If no match is found, a Lead is created.
2. **Ongoing Sync** - Changes made to the Deal in Channeltivity are reflected in Salesforce and vice versa.
3. **Lead Conversion Handling** - Should you decide to convert a Salesforce Lead to an Opportunity, Channeltivity will recognize this and maintain the link to the corresponding record.

## FAQs:

### Can Salesforce Opportunities be imported into Channeltivity as Deals?

Yes, Salesforce Opportunities can be imported into Channeltivity as Deal Registrations. Learn more about this topic here: How do I create Deal Registrations from Salesforce Opportunities in my PRM?. 

### Is the integration bi-directional?

Yes, the Deal Registration integration is a true bi-bidirectional integration. Your Deal Registration integration field mappings allow you to determine the data flow between the Deal in Channeltivity and the corresponding Lead/Opportunity in Salesforce. 

### When is a Deal synced to Salesforce?

You can configure the Deal Registration integration settings to sync new Deals to Salesforce manually or automatically based on specific events.  

* **Manual:**Requires an Internal User to manually sync the Deal to Salesforce by clicking the Salesforce button on the Deal in Channeltivity > Sync .
* **Event-Based** (Automatic)**:**Deals are automatically synced to Salesforce when a selected event occurs:
  + Created
  + Pre-Approved
  + Approved

### When does Channeltivity create a Lead vs. an Opportunity in Salesforce?

By default, Channeltivity creates Leads rather than Opportunities. The reason Channeltivity creates Leads instead of Opportunities is because Opportunities have to be associated with an Account and Contact in Salesforce, and every company has its own unique guidelines for establishing those associations. Since the rules vary across companies, we felt it was best to create Leads instead of Opportunities to allow Users to select the relevant Account/Contact when converting the Lead to an Opportunity. 

However, Channeltivity also offers an optional setting that, when enabled, Channeltivity will attempt to match the End User Contact on the Deal to an existing Salesforce Contact based on email. # Best PRM Software in 2026

An honest comparison of the best PRM (partner relationship management) software in 2026 — pricing, CRM integrations, and who each tool is really for.

PRM (Partner Relationship Management) software — also called partner management software or channel partner software — helps you run partner programs — referral, reseller, affiliate, and channel — with a real system behind onboarding, deal registration, partner portals, enablement content, and reporting. If your CRM is built for your direct sales team, a PRM is the equivalent system for your partners.

TL;DR: There’s no single “best PRM software” — the right pick depends on your program size, price sensitivity, and partner motion. Here are the best PRM software options in 2026, grouped by the job they do best:

* Best PRM for SMBs & startups: PartnerPortal, Kiflo
* Best PRM for CRM coverage: PartnerPortal
* Best AI-native PRM: Introw
* Best PRM for many partner types: JourneyBee
* Best PRM for affiliate & referral scale: PartnerStack
* Best PRM for Salesforce/Dynamics customization: Magentrix
* Best PRM for Salesforce: Salesforce PRM
* Best enterprise PRM: Impartner, ZINFI, Unifyr, Allbound / ChannelScaler

## How we picked the best PRM software (methodology)

We didn’t rank on feature-count or on who has the flashiest AI messaging. We weighted four things a real buyer actually lives with:

1. Is it a real PRM? Full partner lifecycle — onboarding, deal/lead registration, portal, enablement, reporting — not just an affiliate-link tracker.
2. CRM integration depth. What actually syncs, how reliably, and which CRMs (not just Salesforce and HubSpot).
3. Time-to-value. Can a normal team launch in days, or does it need a services project and a quarter?
4. Fit for your size and motion. The best enterprise PRM is the wrong tool for most Startups and SMBs, and vice versa.

We deliberately kept the list to genuine PRMs and clearly labeled the edge cases. We didn’t pad it out with affiliate-only tools to hit a bigger number — see Tools we deliberately didn’t rank at the end.

## What changed in PRM software in 2026

* CRM-native is the new baseline. Buyers increasingly expect the PRM to live inside their CRM’s data, not maintain a separate copy — and increasingly for CRMs beyond Salesforce/HubSpot.

Modified on Tue, 3 Feb at 2:33 PM

This article provides an overview of Channeltivity’s Deal Registration integration with Salesforce. Please also see the Deal Registration Salesforce Integration Setup instructions.

Channeltivity’s Deal Registration integration with Salesforce makes it easy to get your Partners’ registered Deals from Channeltivity into your Salesforce CRM. Following the illustration below, the integration can be explained in three steps:

1. **Channeltivity Deal Submission and Salesforce Record Creation** - Once a Partner submits a new Deal registration, Channeltivity creates a copy of the registered Deal as a Lead within Salesforce. This can be configured to happen manually or automatically based on creation or approval status. 
   * **(Optional Setting)** **Opportunity Creation via Contact Match:** If enabled, Channeltivity will attempt to match the End User Contact on the Deal to an existing Salesforce Contact **using the email address**. If exactly**one match is found**, an Opportunity is created instead of a Lead. If no match is found, a Lead is created.
2. **Ongoing Sync** - Changes made to the Deal in Channeltivity are reflected in Salesforce and vice versa.
3. **Lead Conversion Handling** - Should you decide to convert a Salesforce Lead to an Opportunity, Channeltivity will recognize this and maintain the link to the corresponding record.

## FAQs:

### Can Salesforce Opportunities be imported into Channeltivity as Deals?

Yes, Salesforce Opportunities can be imported into Channeltivity as Deal Registrations. Learn more about this topic here: How do I create Deal Registrations from Salesforce Opportunities in my PRM?. 

### Is the integration bi-directional?

Yes, the Deal Registration integration is a true bi-bidirectional integration. Your Deal Registration integration field mappings allow you to determine the data flow between the Deal in Channeltivity and the corresponding Lead/Opportunity in Salesforce. 

### When is a Deal synced to Salesforce?

You can configure the Deal Registration integration settings to sync new Deals to Salesforce manually or automatically based on specific events.  

* **Manual:**Requires an Internal User to manually sync the Deal to Salesforce by clicking the Salesforce button on the Deal in Channeltivity > Sync .
* **Event-Based** (Automatic)**:**Deals are automatically synced to Salesforce when a selected event occurs:
  + Created
  + Pre-Approved
  + Approved

### When does Channeltivity create a Lead vs. an Opportunity in Salesforce?

By default, Channeltivity creates Leads rather than Opportunities. The reason Channeltivity creates Leads instead of Opportunities is because Opportunities have to be associated with an Account and Contact in Salesforce, and every company has its own unique guidelines for establishing those associations. Since the rules vary across companies, we felt it was best to create Leads instead of Opportunities to allow Users to select the relevant Account/Contact when converting the Lead to an Opportunity.
